group: Aura Battler Dunbine / The Wings of Rean / Brain Powerd
note: Researched 2026-10-02. Fandom page HTML is behind Cloudflare, so wikitext and page titles came from the MediaWiki API of the Super Robot Wars Wiki (superrobotwars.fandom.com), the Dunbine wiki (byston-well.fandom.com, mostly empty stubs) and the Mecha and Monsters wiki (mmecha.fandom.com), and were checked against English Wikipedia, MAHQ and Akurasu's ACE2 Mech Database. Neither fandom wiki has its own page for most characters: the SRW Wiki keeps them on the list page 'Aura Battler Dunbine/Characters', and the Dunbine wiki has only 'Sho Zama' and 'Cham Huau'. Where no wiki page title exists I used the most widely used English form and gave the variants. The series' official English title is 'Brain Powerd' (no second 'e'). Two names in the request are outside this group: Lilith Fau is from Heavy Metal L-Gaim and Braver is from Blue Comet SPT Layzner. Both are kept here and flagged.

entries.role: Protagonist; Holy Warrior (Seisenshi) from Tokyo summoned to Byston Well; defects from Drake Luft to the resistance; pilots Dunbine, later Billbine
entries.personality: Hot-blooded, stubborn young motocross racer who grows into a serious, driven warrior. Has huge Aura Power but struggles to control it. Has unspoken feelings for Marvel.
entries.notes: Contested. The Dunbine wiki page title and Wikipedia both give 'Shō Zama', which is 'Sho Zama' in plain ASCII. Wikipedia's ACE2 article also uses 'Sho Zama'. Variants: 'Show Zama' (SRW Wiki character list, ADV-era fan usage, Akurasu ACE2 database), 'Shou Zama' (MAHQ). I chose 'Sho Zama' because the series wiki's page title wins.

entries.ja: マーベル・フローズン
entries.role: Holy Warrior from a ranching family near Dallas, Texas; resistance pilot (House Givun); pilots Dunbine in ACE2
entries.personality: Confident, kind and level-headed. A skilled pilot who first meets Sho as an enemy and talks him into questioning Drake. She loves Sho and wishes he would admit his feelings.
entries.notes: Every source checked (SRW Wiki, Wikipedia, MAHQ, Akurasu) spells it 'Marvel Frozen'. A literal romanization would be 'Maaberu Furoozun'. No real competing English form was found.

entries.role: Mi Ferario (fairy) companion of Sho
entries.personality: Tiny, noisy and emotional; Sho's cheerleader. She sides with him loudly against enemies and critics and senses tension before anyone else.
entries.notes: The Dunbine wiki page title is 'Cham Huau', and the SRW Wiki and Wikipedia agree. Variant: 'Cham Fau', the literal reading of ファウ, used by some fan wikis and SRW fan translations. Huau is a ferario surname spelling ('The Story of Huau Huau' on the Dunbine wiki).

entries.role: Masked identity of Burn Bunnings, Drake's former commander, after Sho defeats him; Sho's rival; pilots Zwarth and Galava in ACE2
entries.personality: Once proud and respected, now bitter and obsessed with revenge on Sho. Cold, theatrical, and hides his face behind a mask.
entries.notes: 'Black Knight' is the standard translation of 黒騎士 (Wikipedia, Akurasu, SRW Wiki). The man behind the mask, バーン・バニングス, is spelled 'Burn Bunnings' (SRW Wiki), 'Burne Bannings' (Wikipedia) or 'Bern Bunnings' (MAHQ). His real name is spoiler-sensitive, so check whether the game ever shows it before using it.

entries.role: Holy Warrior from the second group summoned by Drake (said to be from Dublin, Ireland); enemy ace who pilots Leprechaun and is the first to go 'Hyper'
entries.personality: Violent, impulsive and bloodthirsty; enjoys destruction. Her enormous, unstable Aura Power mirrors what Sho could have become.
entries.notes: Contested. The SRW Wiki character list and Wikipedia both spell it 'Jeryll Coochibie', so I used that. Variants: 'Jerryl Coochibi' (Wikipedia ACE2 article), 'Jeryll Cocobee' (Akurasu ACE2 database), 'Jeril Coochibi', and 'Jeryl Kuchibi' (the literal romanization of ジェリル・クチビ). If the project prefers a literal Hepburn form, 'Jeryl Kuchibi' is the clean alternative, but no wiki uses it as a title.

entries.role: Last surviving fairy (Mirauli) of the Pentagona World; companion to Daba Myroad
entries.personality: Cheerful, chatty little fairy who loves Daba's group. No use in a fight, but a good cook and a loyal friend. She is a deliberate homage to Cham.
entries.notes: Misgrouped: リリス・ファウ is from Heavy Metal L-Gaim, not Dunbine. She shares a design and a voice actor (Maria Kawamura) with Cham, so move her to the L-Gaim group. Spelling: the SRW Wiki says just 'Lilith', Wikipedia says 'Lillith Fuau', and common fan or tag usage is 'Lilith Fau'. I chose 'Lilith Fau' because it parallels the Japanese ファウ. Merge with the L-Gaim researcher's result.

entries.role: Queen of the Kingdom of Na; commands the aura battleship Gran-Garan; gives Sho the Billbine
entries.personality: Serene, dignified young queen with strong Aura Power and a sense of duty to all of Byston Well. Calm but resolute.
entries.notes: Contested. 'Ciela Lapana' is used by Wikipedia, Behind The Voice Actors and the Bandai HG figure listing on MyFigureCollection. The SRW Wiki character list writes 'Ceila Lapana' (a single list entry, not a page title, and it looks like a transposition). Its Gran-Garan page says just 'Shela'. Other variants: 'Shiela', 'Sheela' and 'Sheila Lapana'. The Japanese シーラ reads 'Shiira'.

entries.role: American Holy Warrior summoned with Sho; fights for Drake and later Bishot Hate; pilots Wryneck in ACE2
entries.personality: Brash and proud. At first he treats Byston Well as a game, then becomes obsessed with beating Sho to save his pride. Makes poor choices.
entries.notes: Consistent across the SRW Wiki, Wikipedia and MAHQ. Minor variant: 'Todd Guiness' (one 'n', on the mmecha wiki).

entries.ja: ガラリア・ニャムヒー
entries.role: Knight in Burn's squadron of Drake's army; pilots Drumlo, Virunvee and Bastole
entries.personality: Fiercely ambitious and hot-tempered. Desperate to win glory and restore her family name, which was disgraced when her parents defected. Has a rivalry with Sho.
entries.notes: Neither fandom wiki has a page for her. 'Garalia Nyamhee' is used by Wikipedia, MAHQ, Behind The Voice Actors and Akurasu. Variants seen: 'Galalia', 'Gararia', and 'Nyamuhee' or 'Nyamuhi' (the literal reading of ニャムヒー). I rate this medium only because no wiki page title exists. The sources agree with each other.

entries.role: Main antagonist; Lord of House Luft in the Kingdom of Ah (アの国), who summons Holy Warriors and wages war to unite Byston Well; commands the Will Wipps
entries.personality: Ambitious, scheming warlord who believes his conquest is justified. Loves his daughter Riml but is blind to the plots around him.
entries.notes: Consistent everywhere. His army is 'Drake's army' or the 'Drake Army' (ドレイク軍).

entries.role: Generic enemy pilot or soldier of Drake Luft's army
entries.notes: Generic label, translated descriptively. No wiki defines it. Alternatives: 'Drake Army Soldier' or 'Drake Trooper'. Keep it in line with the other generic labels (e.g. 'Reclaimer Soldier').

entries.role: Generic officer of Drake Luft's army
entries.notes: Generic label, translated descriptively. Alternative: 'Drake Army Officer'.

entries.role: Protagonist; young man of mixed Japanese-American heritage pulled into Byston Well, where he becomes a Holy Warrior; pilots the Aura Battler Nanajin (and Aka-Nanajin)
entries.personality: Earnest and idealistic, but angry about his place between two countries. Grows into a determined Holy Warrior who opposes Sakomizu's plan.
entries.notes: Wikipedia ('Asap Suzuki', named after the acronym ASAP), the Wikipedia ACE2 article and Akurasu all agree. Variant: 'Aesap Suzuki' (mmecha wiki). The Japanese keeps the given-name-then-surname order (エイサップ鈴木), so English keeps 'Asap Suzuki'. The Wings of Rean fandom wiki pages are empty stubs, so no page title exists.

entries.ja: サコミズ・シンジロウ
entries.role: Antagonist; former WWII Imperial Japanese Ohka (kamikaze) pilot who became King of the Hojo Kingdom in Byston Well; Holy Warrior who holds the Wings of Rean shoes; pilots the Oukaou
entries.personality: Proud, imperious old king haunted by wartime Japan. Charismatic and bitter, set on returning to the surface world on his own terms.
entries.notes: Wikipedia writes 'Shinjirō Sakomizu', which is 'Shinjiro Sakomizu' in ASCII. Akurasu uses 'Shinjirou Sakomizu'. The Japanese label is surname-first (サコミズ・シンジロウ). English uses Western order. The short form 'Sakomizu' matches the in-game label.

entries.role: Female lead; 17-year-old Brain Powerd pilot (Hime Brain) aboard the Novis Noah
entries.personality: Cheerful, warm and motherly toward the children and her Brain. Optimistic and brave, and believes in talking to people and Antibodies alike.
entries.notes: Contested reading. The kanji 宇都宮 are normally read 'Utsunomiya', but in this character's name they read Utsumiya. Wikipedia gives 宇都宮 比瑪, Utsumiya Hime, and the fan wikis and Akurasu all use 'Hime Utsumiya'. Do not use 'Utsunomiya'. The in-game label 比瑪 is 'Hime'.

entries.role: Male lead; former Reclaimer who escapes Orphan and pilots Yuu Brain, later Nelly Brain, for Novis Noah
entries.personality: Brooding lone wolf who resents his scientist parents. Often acts alone, but values life and comes to fight to save his sister Quincy.
entries.notes: Wikipedia's heading, the fan wiki page titles, Akurasu and Wikipedia's ACE2 article all use 'Yuu Isami'. Variants: 'Yu Isami' (Wikipedia section anchors) and 'Yū Isami'. The unit name 'Yuu Brain' uses the same spelling, so keep the two consistent.

entries.ja: ジョナサン・グレーン
entries.role: Reclaimer ace of Orphan; pilots Jonathan Grand Cher, later Jonathan Baronz; Yuu's rival and the son of Novis Noah's captain Anoa McCormick
entries.personality: Arrogant, aggressive and taunting, full of resentment toward Yuu and his own mother. Loyal to Baron Maximilian.
entries.notes: 'Jonathan Glenn' is used by Wikipedia, the official Good Smile product text ('Jonathan Glenn's special version of the Grand Cher') and Akurasu. グレーン could be read 'Gren' or 'Green', but the established form is 'Glenn'. One-off misspelling: 'Glen'.

entries.ja: クインシィ・イッサー
entries.role: Reclaimer leader at Orphan; Yuu's older sister (real name Iiko Isami); pilots Quincy Grand Cher, later Quincy Baronz
entries.personality: Harsh, domineering and emotionally unstable. She denies her past as Iiko and resents Yuu, but underneath she is a lonely, confused girl.
entries.notes: Wikipedia, Akurasu and Wikipedia's ACE2 article all use 'Quincy Issa'. The literal reading of イッサー would be 'Issaa' or 'Isser', so variants include 'Quincy Isser' and 'Quincy Issaa'. Her real name 伊佐未依衣子 is 'Iiko Isami' ('Iko' on mmecha).

entries.ja: バロン・マクシミリアン
entries.role: Masked figure who seizes control of Orphan in Jonathan's name and gives him the Baronz; secretly Anoa McCormick, the missing captain of Novis Noah
entries.personality: Mysterious, theatrical and manipulative. Acts as a mentor to Jonathan, driven by a twisted longing for her estranged son.
entries.notes: Wikipedia's section heading is 'Baron Maximilian', but its nihongo line spells it 'Maximillian' with two l's. I chose the heading form. Gender: the Baron poses as a man ('he'), but the true identity is the woman Anoa McCormick. Treat the identity as a spoiler and check how the ACE2 script refers to the Baron before choosing pronouns.

entries.ja: アイリーン・キャリアー
entries.role: Ship's doctor (also an acupuncturist and former top military officer) on Novis Noah; becomes its captain after Captain McCormick disappears
entries.personality: Calm, capable and motherly; a steady leader the pilots, especially Hime, look up to.
entries.notes: Wikipedia gives 'Irene Carrier' (Airiin Kyariaa). No competing English form was found.

entries.role: Generic Reclaimer pilot (Grand Cher pilot) loyal to Orphan
entries.notes: Generic label, translated descriptively from 'Reclaimer'. Alternative: 'Reclaimer Trooper'.

entries.role: The people who serve Orphan and pilot Grand Chers to gather its plates; plural 'Reclaimers'
entries.notes: 'Reclaimer(s)' in Wikipedia, mmecha and the official Good Smile product text. No variants.

entries.role: Gigantic sentient alien ship buried under the Pacific; its awakening threatens Earth; base of the Reclaimers
entries.notes: 'Orphan' everywhere. A literal reading would be 'Orufan'. Wikipedia refers to it as 'she' in places.

entries.role: Anti-Orphan battleship (carrier with a pyramid superstructure); base of the Brain Powerd pilots
entries.notes: The SRW Wiki, mmecha and the Wikipedia article use 'Novis Noah'. The Wikipedia character list mixes 'Novis Noah', 'Novis Noa' and 'Novis-Noa'. ノア is the Japanese for Noah, so 'Noah' is the reasonable choice. Variant: 'Novis Noa'.

entries.ja: オーガニック・エナジー
entries.role: The life-energy produced by Orphan and the Antibodies (Brain Powerds and Grand Chers); researched by the Isami family
entries.notes: Direct katakana English. The sources write it lowercase ('organic energy', 'organic waves', 'organic engine'). Capitalize it only if the glossary style capitalizes in-universe terms.

entries.role: Drake army mass-production Aura Battler (grunt unit)
entries.notes: The Dunbine wiki page title, the SRW Wiki, MAHQ and mmecha all agree on 'Drumlo'. Rare variant: 'Doramuro'.

entries.role: Drake army Aura Battler (Garalia's and Burn's unit in the series)
entries.notes: The Dunbine wiki page title, the SRW Wiki, MAHQ and Akurasu all use 'Virunvee'. Variant: 'Biranbee' or 'Virunbee', from a literal reading.

entries.role: Drake army Aura Battler (Garalia's pink custom in the series)
entries.notes: Consistent across all sources. Literal variant: 'Bastool'.

entries.role: Heavily armed Drake army Aura Battler; Jeryll's unit in ACE2
entries.notes: Page title on both wikis. Variant: 'Reprakaan' (literal).

entries.role: Late-war Aura Battler of the Drake and Kingdom of Kuh side (Bishot Hate); Todd's unit in ACE2
entries.notes: The Dunbine wiki page title, the SRW Wiki, MAHQ and Wikipedia's ACE2 article all use 'Wryneck', the name of a bird. Literal variant: 'Ryneck'.

entries.role: Giant 'Hyper' form of the Wryneck (boss unit; Todd's hyper-ized Wryneck)
entries.notes: The SRW Wiki and Akurasu both say 'Hyper Wryneck'. The in-game katakana has no separator, so the English is two words.

entries.role: Drake army high-performance Aura Battler
entries.notes: Consistent across all sources. Literal variant: 'Biaresu'.

entries.role: Most powerful late-war Drake Aura Battler; the Black Knight's unit
entries.notes: Page title on both wikis. Don't confuse it with 'Zwauth' (ズワウス), a different unit from the Neo Byston Well OVA.

entries.role: Aura Fighter (not humanoid); the Black Knight's second unit in ACE2
entries.notes: Contested, and a conflict with the rules. The Dunbine wiki has an empty stub page titled 'Gallaba', which the 'wiki wins' rule would favour. But the SRW Wiki, MAHQ, mmecha, Akurasu and Wikipedia's ACE2 article all use 'Galava'. I chose 'Galava' on that consensus. Switch to 'Gallaba' if the project applies the series-wiki rule strictly. The same applies to ハイパーガラバ ('Hyper Galava').

entries.series: Blue Comet SPT Layzner (NOT this group)
entries.role: SPT-BV-15C Braver, a Grados SPT (grunt). It appears among the Layzner units in the ACE2 unit list (between Dargen and Eldar), and a mission objective reads 'destroy all Braver and Dimage'
entries.notes: Misgrouped: not from Dunbine, Wings of Rean or Brain Powerd. The SRW Wiki Layzner mecha list gives 'SPT-BV-15C Braver'. ACE2 shows the name without the model number. Its position in work/translation/en/menu3061.json (next to the other Layzner SPTs) supports this. Move it to the Layzner group.

entries.role: Title Aura Battler; Sho's first unit; Marvel's playable unit in ACE2
entries.notes: Page title on both wikis. No variants.

entries.role: Sho's upgraded, transformable Aura Battler from the Kingdom of Na; Sho's playable unit in ACE2 (also a camouflage-color version)
entries.notes: The Dunbine wiki page title, MAHQ, Wikipedia and Akurasu use 'Billbine'. Variants: 'Bilvine' (the SRW Wiki's own mecha list) and 'Bilbine'. The camo version is 'Billbine (Camouflage Color)' or 'Night Camouflage Billbine'.

entries.series: Aura Battler Dunbine: The Tale of Neo Byston Well (OVA)
entries.role: Legendary Aura Battler of Shion Zaba in the Neo Byston Well OVA (set 700 years after the TV series)
entries.notes: The SRW Wiki and mmecha say 'Sirbine'. Variants: 'Sarbine', 'Servine' and 'Saabine'. The source series is the OVA, not the TV series. I could not confirm what role the Sirbine plays in ACE2.

entries.role: Aura battleship of Queen Ciela Lapana (Kingdom of Na)
entries.notes: The SRW Wiki page title and Wikipedia use 'Gran-Garan'. Variants: 'Gran Garan' (SRW Wiki mecha list), 'Guran Galan' (MAHQ, mmecha) and 'Gulan Gulan' (SRW Wiki character list). I chose the page-title form. The hyphen stands in for the Japanese middle dot.

entries.role: Aura battleship of Elle Humm (Kingdom of Lao), armed with the Aura Nova Cannon
entries.notes: Contested. The SRW Wiki page title is 'Goraon', which matches the katakana ゴラオン. MAHQ, mmecha and Wikipedia write 'Graon'. 'The wiki wins' points to 'Goraon'.

entries.role: Drake Luft's flagship, the first aura battleship
entries.notes: The SRW Wiki mecha list and MAHQ write 'Will Wipps'. Variants: 'Will-Wips' (Wikipedia), 'Wills Wipps' (mmecha) and 'Will Wisps' (Akurasu). No wiki page title exists.

entries.role: The type of Antibody that rebels against Orphan; generic Brain Powerd unit (also the series title)
entries.notes: The official spelling is 'Brain Powerd', without the second 'e'. 'Brain Powered' is a common misspelling, so do not 'correct' it. Plural: 'Brain Powerds'. Individual units are called 'X Brain' (Yuu Brain, Hime Brain).

entries.role: Yuu Isami's Brain Powerd
entries.notes: The SRW Wiki, mmecha, Akurasu and Wikipedia's ACE2 article all use 'Yuu Brain'. Variants: 'Yu Brain' and 'You Brain' (Wikipedia, about model kits). Keep it consistent with 'Yuu Isami'.

entries.role: Hime Utsumiya's Brain Powerd
entries.notes: Consistent across all sources.

entries.role: Orphan-loyal Antibody piloted by Reclaimers (generic grunt unit)
entries.notes: Contested. The official licensed English is 'Grand Cher' (Good Smile MODEROID products), which Wikipedia and mmecha also use. The SRW Wiki's mecha list uses 'Grancher', a straight romanization of グランチャー, but it has no page for the unit. I chose 'Grand Cher'. Use 'Grancher' if the project follows the SRW Wiki list strictly. Whichever you pick applies to every '... Grand Cher' entry below. Plural: 'Grand Chers'.

entries.ja: アーミー・グランチャー
entries.role: Grand Cher flown by US military forces occupying Orphan
entries.notes: mmecha says 'Army Grand Cher'. The SRW Wiki gallery says 'Army Grancher'. Follows the Grand Cher decision.

entries.ja: ジョナサン・グランチャー
entries.role: Jonathan Glenn's custom Grand Cher
entries.notes: mmecha says 'Jonathan Grand Cher', Good Smile says 'Grand Cher (Jonathan's Machine)', and the SRW Wiki says 'Jonathan Grancher'. Follows the Grand Cher decision.

entries.ja: ジョナサングランチャー
entries.role: Same unit as ジョナサン・グランチャー; this game string just has no middle dot
entries.notes: Same unit as the dotted string, so give it the same English. The two strings probably differ only because of display-length limits.

entries.ja: クインシィ・グランチャー
entries.role: Quincy Issa's red custom Grand Cher
entries.notes: mmecha says 'Quincy Grand Cher', Good Smile says 'Grand Cher (Quincy's Machine)', and the SRW Wiki says 'Quincy Grancher'. The Wikipedia character list's 'Quincy Grand' is a truncation. Follows the Grand Cher decision.

entries.ja: ジョナサン・バロンズゥ
entries.role: Evolved Antibody that Baron Maximilian gives to Jonathan Glenn
entries.notes: Contested. mmecha and Akurasu say 'Jonathan Baronz', and Wikipedia's character list says 'Baronz Grand Cher'. The SRW Wiki romanizes it 'Baronzu'. The rare 'Volonth' or 'Volonthe' (Crusade TCG) is described as a mistranslation. I chose 'Baronz'.

entries.ja: クインシィ・バロンズゥ
entries.role: Baronz that evolved from Quincy's Grand Cher; Quincy's playable unit in ACE2
entries.notes: Wikipedia's ACE2 article, Akurasu's ACE2 database and mmecha all say 'Quincy Baronz'. Variants: 'Quincy Baronzu' (SRW Wiki) and 'Quincy Volonthe' (TCG).
